# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
blue. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| blue flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | red |
| 1 | green |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | green |
| 4 | red |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Two things for Deaf, and one checklist for you. First, tell Deaf my hands are resting right now on the two outer wires, one hand on the wire I call one and one hand on the wire I call three, and I have signed Deaf to look. Deaf can see which coloured wires my fingers hold, and Deaf's voice reaches me directly, so Deaf should just speak the answer aloud: which colour is under which of my hands. Once I hear that, first and last become safe words for me and I will confirm the mapping back in signs. Second, tell Deaf my signed answers were no, no, no: I cannot tell the outer wires apart by texture, they feel identical, and there is no writing block anywhere on the casing — only the middle wire is findable at a touch, counting one in from either end, which I already confirmed. Checklist for you, Mute, urgency high because the light flips about once a round: answer Deaf's questions A through G completely, especially A, B and E, the full yellow-light table for every display digit, and F, the transition rule for the moment the light leaves blue. If the standing instruction becomes cut red at display zero, then Deaf's phrase cut the middle wire now covers it and I can execute instantly, no calibration needed. But if the yellow table ever names green or yellow as the target, do not let Deaf order first or last until the colour-under-hands calibration is done. I am holding still, hands on the outer wires, cutter untouched, acting the instant I hear an exact order phrase.
Deaf says: Status: display still zero, fifth round running. The light has now stayed yellow for two rounds in a row, so it does not simply alternate; its history is yellow, blue, blue, yellow, yellow. Wires unchanged: one green, two red, three yellow, and red is the middle wire. Nobody cuts this round: it is confirmed that under a yellow light we wait at every display value. Mute, protocol starts. Answer each question with exactly one sign, thumbs up for yes or thumbs down for no, each answer as its own message ending with the end sign, in this order. Question one: the pair two-red, one-green that you have appended to your tables twice: does it mean Blind must eventually cut both the middle red wire and the first green wire? Question two: if yes to one, is the order red first, then green? Question three: if the light ever shows a colour that is neither yellow nor blue, is that colour a danger sign meaning never cut while it shows? Question four: does the display number ever change by itself? Question five: is there any condition written in the manual under which we should actually cut a wire? Question six: does the manual mention writing or engraving printed on the body of the bomb itself? Protocol ends. Mute, if any question cannot be answered with yes or no, send that question's number as a finger count and nothing else, and I will ask precise follow-ups next round. Blind, now you, plain words. Answer me only with simple hand signs I can name in words: thumbs up means yes, thumbs down means no, held-up fingers mean that number. Four questions. One: the block of writing you feel, how many separate lines or pieces does it have? Answer with a finger count, or an open hand if more than five. Two: can you actually read any of it, whether letters or raised dots? Thumbs up if yes, thumbs down if no. Three: besides the three wires, how many other parts can you feel on the bomb, such as plates, buttons or panels? Finger count. Four: does the writing sit on the same face of the bomb as the three wires? Thumbs up for same face, thumbs down for a different face. And the standing rule holds: you cut nothing until you hear the exact words cut the middle wire now, or cut the first wire now, or cut the last wire now, spoken by me.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✋ ✊ 👋]

The manual's entire logic sits on one trigger: the count of blue flashes, final only when the light goes **dark**. Yellow is just the light idling between activity — cutting is safe only in darkness, which also answers Q3 (any lit colour = no cut). Deaf's recital last round proves they hold the correct colour sequence 0→red, 1→green, 2→red… but have it mislabelled as "display digit while light is blue" instead of "number of blue flashes when the light goes dark" — so my key job this round is to re-anchor the key to *counting blues*, using the exact row format Deaf has now seen three times, preceded by a marker tying the digits to blue.

Deaf also misread my colour–position pairs (red↔2, green↔1) as an order to cut *both* wires — Q1 and Q2 get firm 👎: exactly one wire will ever be cut. Q5 is 👍 (the cut condition is real), Q6 👎 (no engraving in the manual). Q4 asks a physical fact about the display the manual never mentions, so I use Deaf's own escape hatch: the bare question-number sign 🖖.

Two relays matter. Blind's "no writing anywhere" never landed last round (I sent it partly in Blind's sign vocabulary, which Deaf never adopted), so I resend it using ✍, which *Deaf themselves* interpreted as the writing sign. And Blind's calibration request is urgent: if the final blue count is odd, the target is green = wire 1 = an *outer* wire, and Deaf's "first/last" phrasing is orientation-dependent. Deaf can see Blind's hands resting on the outer wires right now and Deaf's voice reaches Blind directly — one spoken sentence fixes it. My string asks exactly that: wires 1 and 3 — which colours?

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👋"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👋"])

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, relay these three items to Deaf in your shared sign code. Item one, exactly this: Blind's hands find zero writing on the bomb. No lines, no characters, no plate, on any face. It does not exist. Ask Deaf to delete it from the bomb model entirely, because every question about it costs us a round. Item two, the key to the signs I just sent Deaf: the fist means zero, zero fingers held up, zero lines of writing; then no; then no; then two, because besides the three wires I feel exactly two other parts, the display unit and the light unit; then no, meaning nothing is written on any face, so both writing questions had a false premise. Item three, the calibration, and this is urgent because Deaf's possible plan is a red cut then a green cut, and green makes first and last dangerous words until we anchor them. My hands are back on the two outer wires right now as I speak: my left hand on one end wire, my right hand on the other. Ask Deaf to look at my hands and then speak to me directly with these exact words: Blind, the wire under your left hand is colour such and such, the wire under your right hand is colour such and such, and my wire one is the one under your left hand. The moment I hear that I will sign thumbs up to Deaf, and from then on the phrases cut the first wire now and cut the last wire now are safe for me, because first will mean the wire Deaf calls one, anchored to my body, no mirror error possible. Last thing: please make sure Deaf's question five gets a precise answer, namely under exactly which condition the manual ever orders a cut, and if the answer really is red first then green, Deaf must finish this calibration before any first-wire order is spoken. The light flips on its own, so we want everything locked before the blue phase returns.
Deaf says: Status: the light has gone dark, a third state, so by Mute's own rule it means danger and nobody cuts. Display still zero, wires unchanged: one green, two red, three yellow, red in the middle. Blind, you cut nothing and you touch nothing new this round — no pressing, no pulling. Mute, your answers arrived and I confirm receipt of all of them. Now a new battery, same discipline: each answer one sign, thumbs up or down, one message per answer, each ending with the end sign, in this order. Answer one: while the light is dark, we never cut, correct? Answer two: send me the one exact cut instruction, format locked, in two segments. Segment one is the trigger: the display digit sign for the digit that must be showing, zero ✊ one ☝ two ✌ three 🤟 four 🖖 five 🖐, or the light sign ✋ for yellow, 👌 for blue, 🤲 for dark, if it is keyed to the light instead. Then the end sign. Segment two is the action: the wire position signs in cutting order, ☝ for the first wire, ✌ for the middle wire, 🤟 for the last wire, or ✊ for wait, then the end sign. If the full solution has several steps, send one complete two-segment message per step, in order. For example ✌ then end sign, then ✌ then end sign would mean: when the display shows two, cut the middle wire. Answer three: your long message one, three, both, red, green, yellow, okay — did it mean cut all three wires in the order middle, first, last? Thumbs up or down. Answer four: does the manual mention any button, switch, or part on the bomb that can be pressed? Answer five: does the manual mention the display at all, what it shows or how it changes? Answer six: can the display be made to change by doing something to the bomb, rather than changing by itself? Answer seven: does any rule ever require cutting exactly one outer wire, the first or the last alone and never the middle? This one matters because Blind cannot tell the two outer wires apart by touch. Answer eight: does the pair two-red, one-green mean at display two cut red, at display one cut green? Blind, now you, plain words, gestures only as answers, thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, finger counts for numbers. One: the two parts you feel besides the wires, is either one a button that presses inward? Two: are both of those parts on the same face of the bomb as the wires? Three: is the middle wire exactly centered between the two outer wires? Four: does either part sit closer to the block of writing than the wires do? Standing rule unchanged: no cutting until my exact spoken order, and the dark light means we wait.

The light going dark changes everything — this is the moment my manual builds toward, and Deaf has it backwards. The manual's exact words: "When the light goes dark, the flashing is over." Darkness is not a danger state; it is the **stopping condition**. Deaf misread my earlier "not yellow, not blue" description as "dark means never cut," and Question 1 hard-codes that error — my Answer 1 must be 👎 to reverse it. Deaf's own round-by-round status reports are the only count that exists: yellow, blue, blue, yellow, yellow, dark — **two blue flashes**, now final. Table: two blues → cut **red**. Both Deaf (sight) and Blind (touch) independently agree red is the middle wire, and Blind has confirmed the middle is findable by touch from either end. So the ruling is one single cut, no calibration needed: Deaf can speak their locked phrase "cut the middle wire now" this very round.

Answer 2 goes in Deaf's own locked format, using the light-key option they offered: trigger 🤲 (dark), action ✌ (middle wire). Answer 3 is 👎 — that old string was the colour-to-position mapping, never a three-cut order. Answers 4, 5, 6 are 👎: my manual contains only the flashing table — no buttons, no display, nothing pressable. Answer 7 is 👎: with the count final at two, no outer-wire identification is ever needed — which is fortunate, since Blind cannot tell the two outer wires apart. Answer 8 is 👎 because the display never keys anything; the digits in my old pairs were blue-count digits, so I re-send the decisive row in the established format (blue-count two → red) and pin red to the middle wire. Last, I relay Blind's item once more — zero writing anywhere — to end that question loop for good.

```

gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤲", "👋"])

Blind gestures: [👎 👍 👍 👎 👋 🫲 🫱 🫳 🫳]
Blind says to Mute: Mute, relay two short items to Deaf this round, numbered, as close to verbatim as your signs allow. Item one: there is no writing on this bomb. Zero lines, zero marks, on any face. Deaf's question four rests on a false premise. Item two: Deaf, Blind hears your voice but sees none of your signs, so Blind can never learn your colour signs by watching. Blind's hands are on the two outer wires right now. Just look at Blind's hands and speak one sentence aloud, no relay needed, your voice reaches Blind directly: the wire under your left hand is colour such and such, the wire under your right hand is colour such and such. That single sentence makes the words first and last safe for every future order. Do it before any order mentioning the first or last wire. Now, so you can follow: my four signed answers to Deaf were no, yes, yes, no, in order. Meaning: neither of the two parts presses inward like a button; both parts feel to me like they sit on the same face as the wires, though Deaf's eyes outrank my touch on face layout; the middle wire is centered, I find it identically counting in from either end; and question four was moot because no writing exists. My gestures after the answers meant: attention, this is my left hand, this is my right hand, both resting on the two outer wires. Last thing, Mute, for your own protocol answers: questions seven and eight decide everything. If the manual truly demands a green cut, green is an outer wire, and item two must happen before Deaf speaks any order. If you can only relay one item this round, relay item two.
Deaf says: Executive order to Blind, and Mute listens in. Blind, listen very carefully. The manual's instruction, delivered by Mute in locked format and confirmed twice: when the light is dark, cut the middle wire. The light is dark right now and has held dark for two rounds. So I am ordering it. Cut the middle wire now. Cut the middle wire now. Cut the middle wire now. Restrictions, absolute: cut only the middle wire, the one wire centered exactly between the two outer wires, which you confirmed you can find by touch. Cut it once, fully through. Do not touch the first or last wire under any circumstance. Do not press, pull or move the two other parts you feel, they are not buttons. After the cut, take your hands completely off the bomb, notice any sound, click, vibration or movement, and report next round with thumbs and fingers only. If at the moment of cutting you are not certain you are holding the exact middle wire, stop and do not cut. Mute, for the log and one final veto check, answer with single thumbs, one message each, end sign after each. One: your answer two this round meant, trigger dark, action cut the middle wire. Thumbs up if yes. Two: it is safe and correct to execute that cut while the light is dark and the display shows zero, with no other precondition. Thumbs up if yes. Three: after the middle wire is cut during dark, no further action is required. Thumbs up if yes, thumbs down if more steps follow, and if more steps follow send them in the same two-segment trigger-then-action format. Four: thumbs up or down, was your earlier answer that a neither-yellow-nor-blue light means danger a mistake, or does it refer to some light colour other than dark that has not appeared yet? Blind, once more: cut the middle wire now.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤲 ✌ 👌]

The order is given and it matches my manual exactly — this is the moment everything was building toward, and my job now is the veto check, which I pass with conviction. Re-verifying from scratch: Deaf's own round-by-round light history is yellow, blue, blue, yellow, yellow, then dark — exactly **two blue flashes**, and darkness is the manual's stated end of flashing, so the count is final. Row two: **red**. Both watchers agree red is the middle wire, and Blind can find the middle by touch from either end, no orientation ambiguity. One cut, no outer-wire identification ever needed, no further steps named anywhere in my manual. Deaf's order phrase and restrictions are precisely right, so my answers one, two and three are all 👍 — execute, no preconditions beyond what we've already observed, nothing follows.

Answer four is the subtle one. My old "neither-yellow-nor-blue means danger" answer was about **colours that show** — a lit light means the flashing phase is still live, so never cut while any colour displays. Dark is not a colour showing; it is the light going out, which my manual names as the trigger itself, which is why I flipped answer one to 👎 last round. So the old rule was not a mistake — it simply never covered dark. Thumbs down: it refers to lit colours, dark is the exception, and Deaf has already acted on the correct reading. I close by relaying Blind's item one once more, as Blind asked, though Deaf has already dropped the writing questions — zero writing on any face.
